look_here_first: Start with life cycle and the bracts. Texas paintbrush is an annual, usually with bright red to orange-red showy bracts and a more compact spring-flowering habit than the perennial prairie paintbrushes.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Exact target-zone county documentation: Travis, Williamson, Hays.

best_field_traits: upper leaves/bracts brightly red to orange-red
showy color comes mainly from bracts rather than petals
morphology_keys.comparison_training: C. purpurea and C. lindheimeri are perennial. C. indivisa is the annual Texas paintbrush and usually looks more compact and uniformly scarlet-red.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. purpurea and C. lindheimeri are perennial. C. indivisa is the annual Texas paintbrush and usually looks more compact and uniformly scarlet-red.
